name: Ricardo A. Zamora
affiliation: Instituto de Investigación Interdisciplinaria (I3) and Center for Bioinformatics, Simulation and Modeling (CBSM), Universidad de Talca
note: Chemist and biochemist working on redox proteins and light-controlled drugs: photoswitchable compounds aimed at the antioxidant defences tumours rely on, and redox proteins redesigned as photomodulable chimeras. The photochemistry and the redox biochemistry in our shared projects are his.

name: Jeffrey R. Comer
affiliation: Nanotechnology Innovation Center of Kansas State (NICKS), Kansas State University
note: Simulates the interface between nanotechnology and biology, and transport in living systems. His specialty is the free energy of adsorption, what it costs a molecule to stick to a nanomaterial, to leave it or to cross a membrane, which is the number behind much of our own work on surfaces.

name: Riccardo Alessandri
note: Builds coarse-grained models of soft matter, within the Martini force field initiative, to follow how ions, electrons and small molecules travel through polymers. Those models reach sizes and times that all-atom simulation cannot, which is exactly what a whole nanoparticle meeting a membrane demands.

name: Cristián Vilos
position: Full Professor, Departamento de Ciencias Preclínicas
affiliation: Center for Nanomedicine, Diagnostics and Drug Development (ND3), Facultad de Medicina, Universidad de Talca
note: Experimental nanomedicine: his group designs polymeric and lipopolymeric nanoparticles for targeted delivery, measures how they behave against blood and cells, and works on combination therapy for colorectal cancer. He makes and tests the carriers we model.

name: Alexis Aspée
affiliation: Facultad de Química y Biología, Universidad de Santiago de Chile
note: Physical chemist of free radicals and excited states. He works with fluorescent and pre-fluorescent probes, time-resolved laser techniques for transient species, and the oxidation of amino acids and proteins; the probes we place in simulated membranes come out of that chemistry.
